Why is Jaipur pink? 1876, a royal welcome, and a law that followed.

Jaipur was founded on 18 November 1727 as one of India's earliest planned cities, laid out on a grid. In 1876 Maharaja Sawai Ram Singh II had the old city painted pink, a colour of welcome, for the visiting Prince of Wales. A law in 1877 is said to have made pink compulsory there. In 2017 the city's smart city plan set aside about ₹14.6 crore to restore bazaar facades in the original colour, and in 2019 UNESCO listed the walled city as a World Heritage Site. Some historians think the city was pinkish even before, and 1876 was a repaint.
